question: The area of a square is 16x² + 40x + 25 square units. Find the perimeter of the square.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of square = 16x² + 40x + 25 = (4x)² + 2(4x)(5) + 5² = (4x + 5)².

Side of the square = √(4x + 5)² = 4x + 5.

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × (4x + 5) = 16x + 20.

Taking 2 as a common factor, Perimeter = 2(8x + 10).

**∴ The correct answer is 2(8x + 10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd68c1e109ee446f3b2cc9e922bcf38055809b5dc415c090abf238d3485a672.png] 

**Given:**

Area of the square = 16x² + 40x + 25

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = (Side)²

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

Algebraic Identity: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

**Calculation:**

⇒ (Side)² = 16x² + 40x + 25

⇒ (Side)² = (4x)² + 2 × (4x) × 5 + (5)²

⇒ (Side)² = (4x + 5)²

⇒ Side = 4x + 5

Now, calculate the perimeter:

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × (4x + 5)

⇒ Perimeter = 16x + 20

⇒ Perimeter = 2(8x + 10)

**∴ The correct answer is 2(8x + 10).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard identities include (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². These are frequently used to form perfect squares in geometry problems.

Properties of a Square

All four sides are equal, and each interior angle is 90°. The diagonals are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal is given by the formula d = Side × √2. The area can also be determined directly from the diagonal using the relation Area = d² ÷ 2.
